Worked example 2.8: LCM using prime factors

Find the LCM of 12 and 18.

  1. Step 1: Express each number as a product of prime factors.

  2. Step 2: Identify all the prime factors that must be included in a common multiple.

    Any multiple of 12 must contain: (The factor is included in ; see next line)
    Any multiple of 18 must contain: (The factor is included in ; see previous line)

    A multiple that contains automatically contains . Similarly, a multiple that contains automatically contains .

  3. Step 3: Multiply the prime factors that have to be included in both multiples to get the LCM.
records.answer_text:
Step 1: Express each number as a product of prime factors.

$$\begin{array}{r | r}
 2 & 12 \\
 \hline
 2 & 6 \\
 \hline
 3 & 3 \\
 \hline
 & 1
 \end{array}$$

$$12=2 \times 2 \times 3$$

$$\begin{array}{r | r}
 2 & 18 \\
 \hline
 3 & 9 \\
 \hline
 3 & 3 \\
 \hline
 & 1
 \end{array}$$

$$18=2 \times 3 \times 3$$

Step 2: Identify all the prime factors that must be included in a common multiple.

Any multiple of 12 must contain: $2 \times 2$ (The factor $3$ is included in $3 \times3$; see next line)
Any multiple of 18 must contain: $3 \times 3$ (The factor $2$ is included in $2 \times 2$; see previous line)

A multiple that contains $2\times 2$ automatically contains $2$. Similarly, a multiple that contains $3\times 3$ automatically contains $3$.

Step 3: Multiply the prime factors that have to be included in both multiples to get the LCM.

$$\text{LCM} = 2 \times 2 \times 3 \times 3 = 36$$

Worked example 2.9: LCM using prime factors in index form

Find the LCM of 60 and 45.

  1. Step 1: Express each number as a product of prime factors in index form.

  2. Step 2: List all the prime factors that were used, to the highest index.

    The factor 2 was used and its highest index is two:
    The factor 3 was used and its highest index is two:
    The factor 5 was used:

  3. Step 3: Multiply the prime factors you listed to get the LCM.
records.answer_text:
Step 1: Express each number as a product of prime factors in index form.

$$\begin{array}{r | r}
 2 & 60 \\
 \hline
 2 & 30 \\
 \hline
 3 & 15 \\
 \hline
 5 & 5 \\
 \hline
 & 1
 \end{array}$$

$$60=2^2 \times 3 \times 5$$

$$\begin{array}{r | r}
 3 & 45 \\
 \hline
 3 & 15 \\
 \hline
 5 & 5 \\
 \hline
 & 1
 \end{array}$$

$$45=3^2 \times 5$$

Step 2: List all the prime factors that were used, to the highest index.

The factor 2 was used and its highest index is two: $2^2$
The factor 3 was used and its highest index is two: $3^2$
The factor 5 was used: $5$

Step 3: Multiply the prime factors you listed to get the LCM.

$$\text{LCM} = 2^2 \times 3^2 \times 5 =2 \times 2 \times 3 \times 3 \times 5 = 180$$

Any multiple of 10 must contain: $5$ ($2$ is included in $2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2$ below)
Any multiple of 16 must contain: $2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2$
Any multiple of 18 must contain: $3 \times 3$ ($2$ is included in $2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2$ above)
$$\therefore \text{LCM} = 5 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 3 \times 3 = 720$$

Only common prime factors to lowest index All prime factors to highest index
Smaller than or equal to given numbers Larger than or equal to given numbers

HCF LCM

$$\begin{array}{r | r}
